decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT explicitly assigns 'Y' at visit 12, while its attached CL.AVISIT enumerates visit labels and excludes 'Y'. The native workbook repeats both declarations.

Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT assigns 'Y' if VISITNUM=12, while adlbc.r lines 164-183 (with the End of Treatment rows of lines 155-161 and 187-197) give AVISIT visit labels and never 'Y'. The program computes the final AVISIT, so the document and the reference computation genuinely disagree.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM lists the parts LB.LBTEST, '(', LB.LBSTRESU and ')' with no blank, while adlbc.r line 132 pastes " (" with a blank before the parenthesis. No later step of the program changes PARAM, so the difference is real.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 97-101) concatenates LBTEST and '(' with no blank as section ADLBC.PARAM states, and every difference is that missing blank. The CL.PARAM_ADLBC labels justify the spaced reading that reproduces the reference, which adlbc.r line 132 also computes.

Define-XML ADLBC.BASE gives Method: LB.LBSTNRHI, while adlbc.r lines 142-148 set BASE with derive_var_base from AVAL on the ABLFL record (ABLFL = LBBLFL at line 143). The program never reads LBSTNRHI for BASE, so the document and the reference computation disagree.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 299-305) copies LB.LBSTNRHI as section ADLBC.BASE states, and the patterns put the upper limit where the reference holds a baseline lab value. The label 'Baseline Value' and CL.AVISITN '0 = Baseline' justify the baseline-AVAL reading that reproduces the reference, as adlbc.r lines 142-148 compute it.

Define-XML ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE with no exception, while adlbc.r line 150 sets CHG missing on every VISITNUM 1 record after derive_var_chg. That exception is part of the final CHG and no document states it.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 193-203) computes AVAL - BASE as section ADLBC.CHG states, and every difference is a missing reference CHG where the literal gives 0. The reading that blanks VISITNUM 1, as adlbc.r line 150 does, reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO states Significant digits: 1, while adlbc.r line 220 stores AVAL / A1LO unrounded and no later step before xportr_write rounds it. The R2A1LO CR-5 evidence confirms the reference holds the unrounded ratio.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 204-214) rounds AVAL / A1LO to one decimal as section ADLBC.R2A1LO states, and every difference is an unrounded reference ratio beside its rounding. The unrounded reading, matching adlbc.r line 220, reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI states Significant digits: 1, while adlbc.r line 221 stores AVAL / A1HI unrounded and no later step before xportr_write rounds it. The R2A1HI CR-5 evidence confirms the reference holds the unrounded ratio.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 215-225) rounds AVAL / A1HI to one decimal as section ADLBC.R2A1HI states, and every difference is an unrounded reference ratio beside its rounding. The unrounded reading, matching adlbc.r line 221, reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states AVAL / A1LO at baseline, while adlbc.r line 222 divides BASE by the A1LO of the current record. The two state the denominator differently, although the reading with the current limit and the literal probe differ only in rounding on this data.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states Significant digits: 1, while adlbc.r line 222 stores BASE / A1LO unrounded and no later step before xportr_write rounds it. The BR2A1LO CR-5 evidence confirms the reference holds the unrounded ratio.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 69-75 and 226-236) takes both operands from the CL.AVISITN 0 = Baseline record and rounds to one decimal as section ADLBC.BR2A1LO states. Every difference is an unrounded reference ratio beside its rounding, and the unrounded current-limit reading of adlbc.r line 222 reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states AVAL / A1HI at baseline, while adlbc.r line 223 divides BASE by the A1HI of the current record. The two state the denominator differently, although the reading with the current limit and the literal probe differ only in rounding on this data.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states Significant digits: 1, while adlbc.r line 223 stores BASE / A1HI unrounded and no later step before xportr_write rounds it. The BR2A1HI CR-5 evidence confirms the reference holds the unrounded ratio.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 69-75 and 237-247) takes both operands from the CL.AVISITN 0 = Baseline record and rounds to one decimal as section ADLBC.BR2A1HI states. Every difference is an unrounded reference ratio beside its rounding, and the unrounded current-limit reading of adlbc.r line 223 reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL takes the maximum of the signed terms LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN) and (.5*LLN) - LBSTRESN, while adlbc.r lines 224-226 take the absolute value of each term before keeping the larger. That changes the final ALBTRVAL, so the statements genuinely differ.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states Significant digits: 3, while adlbc.r line 226 stores the larger absolute term unrounded and no later step before xportr_write rounds it. The ALBTRVAL CR-5 evidence confirms the reference is unrounded.

The literal probe (adlbc-documented-rules.yaml lines 248-274) keeps the larger signed term at three digits, with ULN and LLN read as the LB limits that sections ADLBC.A1HI and ADLBC.A1LO name, and it differs from the reference on nearly every record. The absolute-value reading of adlbc.r lines 224-226 reproduces the reference.
ADLBC.ANRIND's low branch assigns 'Y', while its own CL.LNH enumerates only L, N and H. The full native method retains the same incompatible assignment.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND assigns 'Y' when AVAL < 0.5*LBSTNRLO, while adlbc.r line 227 assigns 'L' in that branch and line 228 only resets missing AVAL to 'N'. The final ANRIND therefore never holds the documented 'Y'.
Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND compares AVAL with 0.5*LBSTRNHI for 'H', while adlbc.r line 227 compares it with 1.5 * LBSTNRHI. Both the multiplier and the source name differ in the final ANRIND.

ADLBC.BNRIND's method literally assigns ANRIND='Y' in its low branch. ADLBC.ANRIND's CL.LNH excludes Y, so the quoted assignment contradicts the named target's permitted values even before repairing BNRIND's target name.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND assigns 'Y' when BASE < 0.5*LBSTNRLO, while adlbc.r lines 231-235 carry the baseline record's ANRIND into BNRIND and line 227 sets that ANRIND to 'L' below half the lower limit. The final BNRIND therefore never holds the documented 'Y'.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND compares BASE with 0.5*LBSTRNHI for 'H', while the baseline ANRIND that adlbc.r lines 231-235 copy into BNRIND compares with 1.5 * LBSTNRHI at line 227. The multiplier and source name differ in the final BNRIND.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT's method assigns 'Y' at VISITNUM=12 or to a discontinued subject's last assessment, while base-ord (adlbc_v3.yaml lines 528-550) maps LB.VISIT to visit labels such as 'Baseline' and leaves other visits blank. The executable rule differs from that method, though it agrees with the attached CL.AVISIT labels.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT's method assigns 'Y', whereas base-eot (adlbc_v1.yaml line 708) assigns 'End of Treatment'. CL.AVISIT lists that label, which supports the specification as a correction but does not remove the difference from the method.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT's method selects the VISITNUM=12 record, and the last assessment only for a subject who discontinues before VISIT 12. The base-eot filter _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE = 1 (adlbc_v1.yaml line 669, computed at lines 810-820) keeps the highest-LBSEQ WEEK 2 to WEEK 24 record of every subject and parameter, with no VISITNUM or discontinuation test.

Section ADLBC.ADY names LB.LBDY, but ADY (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 327-333) computes study_day from _ADT_DATE and TRTSDT and never reads LB.LBDY. The evidence shows both agree on every record, so this is a divergence of source only.

Section ADLBC.VISITNUM states Significant digits: 1, which base-ord rounds to (adlbc_v3.yaml lines 555-558), but base-eot copies ONLY(LB.VISITNUM) unrounded (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 683-684). The comment at adlbc_v3.yaml lines 551-554 relies on End of Treatment sources having whole visit numbers, so the values agree on this data and the difference is a divergence only.

Section ADLBC.PARAM concatenates LB.LBTEST and LB.LBSTRESU, while _PARAM_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 541-563, and the base-eot case at lines 711-749) maps LB.LBTESTCD to fixed labels with a blank before '('. Both the source and the separator differ.

CL.PARAM_ADLBC in section ADLBC.PARAM lists a 'change from previous visit, relative to normal range' label for each analyte, but _PARAM_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 541-563) and the base-eot case (lines 711-749) produce only the standard labels. No row of adlbc_v1.yaml or adlbc_v3.yaml creates that family.

ADRG page-12 describes a second parameter set of change from previous visit relative to normal range values. Neither base-ord (adlbc_v1.yaml line 464) nor base-eot (line 663) nor any adlbc_v3.yaml row creates it.

CL.PARAMN_ADLBC in section ADLBC.PARAMN codes 118 to 135 for the change-from-previous-visit labels, but _PARAMN_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 564-586, base-eot lines 750-788) maps only codes 18 to 35. The specification has no counterpart for those entries.

Section ADLBC.AVAL states Significant digits: 5, but AVAL copies _AVAL_BASE, LB.LBSTRESN (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 370 and 587), without rounding, and adlbc_v3.yaml line 317 records the precision only as submission metadata. The literal probe's rounding matches the reference, so this divergence agrees on this data.

ADRG page-12 describes a second parameter set of change from previous visit relative to normal range values, but neither base-ord (adlbc_v1.yaml line 464) nor base-eot (line 663) nor any adlbc_v3.yaml row derives an AVAL for it. The PARAM.CR-5 evidence shows only the standard labels in the published data too, so the specification matches the data but not the document.

Section ADLBC.BASE names LB.LBSTNRHI, while BASE reads _BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 375 and 588-606), the LB.LBSTRESN of the ABLFL = 'Y' record carried forward. The specification never reads the documented source, a real difference rather than a paraphrase.

Section ADLBC.BASE states Significant digits: 5, but _BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 602-606) carries the analysis value without rounding, and adlbc_v3.yaml line 327 records the precision only as submission metadata. No other element of the specification rounds BASE.

Section ADLBC.CHG states Significant digits: 5, but CHG (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 377-385) subtracts without rounding. adlbc_v3.yaml line 339 records significant_digits: 5 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.

base-ord copies A1LO: LB.LBSTNRLO directly (adlbc_v1.yaml line 478) and base-eot reads ONLY(LB.LBSTNRLO) over one LB record (lines 665-668 and 689-690), the source section ADLBC.A1LO names. The column element has no derivation of its own, but the specification does read the documented copy source, and the evidence shows no difference.

base-ord copies A1HI: LB.LBSTNRHI directly (adlbc_v1.yaml line 479) and base-eot reads ONLY(LB.LBSTNRHI) over one LB record (lines 665-668 and 691-692), the source section ADLBC.A1HI names. The column element has no derivation of its own, but the specification does read the documented copy source, and the evidence shows no difference.

Section ADLBC.R2A1LO states Significant digits: 1, but R2A1LO (adlbc_v1.yaml line 397) divides without rounding. adlbc_v3.yaml line 375 records significant_digits: 1 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.

Section ADLBC.R2A1HI states Significant digits: 1, but R2A1HI (adlbc_v1.yaml line 402) divides without rounding. adlbc_v3.yaml line 387 records significant_digits: 1 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.

Section ADLBC.BR2A1LO's 'at baseline' applies to the whole ratio, but BR2A1LO (adlbc_v1.yaml line 407) divides _BASE by the current record's A1LO. The numerator is taken at baseline while the limit is not.

Section ADLBC.BR2A1LO states Significant digits: 1, but BR2A1LO (adlbc_v1.yaml line 407) divides without rounding. adlbc_v3.yaml line 399 records significant_digits: 1 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.

Section ADLBC.BR2A1HI's 'at baseline' applies to the whole ratio, but BR2A1HI (adlbc_v1.yaml line 412) divides _BASE by the current record's A1HI. The numerator is taken at baseline while the limit is not.

Section ADLBC.BR2A1HI states Significant digits: 1, but BR2A1HI (adlbc_v1.yaml line 412) divides without rounding. adlbc_v3.yaml line 411 records significant_digits: 1 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.

Section ADLBC.ANL01FL flags every record equal to max(ALBTRVAL), so tied maxima all receive Y. _ANL01_RANK (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 302-316) breaks ties by analysis visit, date and LBSEQ, so only one of them can reach rank 1.

Section ADLBC.ALBTRVAL subtracts 1.5*ULN from LBSTRESN, while _T1 (adlbc_v1.yaml line 618) subtracts the analysis value from 1.5*A1HI. The term has the opposite sign, which changes which term is the maximum.

Section ADLBC.ALBTRVAL subtracts LBSTRESN from .5*LLN, while _T2 (adlbc_v1.yaml line 619) subtracts 0.5*A1LO from the analysis value. The term has the opposite sign, which changes which term is the maximum.

Section ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states Significant digits: 3, but the greatest of _T1 and _T2 (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 620-624) is not rounded. adlbc_v3.yaml line 436 records significant_digits: 3 only as submission metadata, which does not round the value.
Section ADLBC.ANRIND's low branch assigns 'Y', while _ANRIND_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 635-636) assigns 'L'. The specification follows CL.LNH rather than the method's text.

Section ADLBC.ANRIND tests AVAL > [0.5*LBSTRNHI), while _ANRIND_BASE (adlbc_v1.yaml line 633) tests AVAL / A1HI > 1.5 with A1HI read from LB.LBSTNRHI. Both the multiplier and the named variable differ.

Section ADLBC.BNRIND's low branch assigns ANRIND = 'Y', while the specification assigns 'L' (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 635-636) to the baseline record's indicator that BNRIND carries (lines 638-656). Both the target and the value differ.
Section ADLBC.BNRIND tests BASE > [0.5*LBSTRNHI), while the baseline record's indicator (adlbc_v1.yaml line 633) tests the ratio to A1HI above 1.5. Both the multiplier and the named variable differ.

Section ADLBC.AENTMTFL tests VISITNUM=12, while AENTMTFL (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 442-445) flags every End of Treatment row and the highest-LBSEQ WEEK 2 to WEEK 24 record (lines 607-616), with no VISITNUM test. A WEEK 24 record is flagged only when it is that last eligible record, so the clause is stated differently, not restated.

Section ADLBC.AENTMTFL limits the last-assessment branch to subjects who discontinue before VISIT 12, but neither AENTMTFL (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 437-446) nor _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (lines 607-616) tests discontinuation. No element of adlbc_v1.yaml or adlbc_v3.yaml reads a discontinuation source.

Section ADLBC.AENTMTFL asks for the last assessment of the analyte, while _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 613-614) takes the highest LBSEQ. A sequence number rather than an assessment date or visit decides which record is last, which is a real difference.

Section ADLBC.LBSTRESN states Significant digits: 5, but base-ord copies LB.LBSTRESN (adlbc_v1.yaml line 477) and base-eot ONLY(LB.LBSTRESN) (lines 687-688) without rounding, and adlbc_v3.yaml line 518 records the precision only as submission metadata. The literal probe's rounding matches the reference, so this divergence agrees on this data.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1391-1393 give IT.ADLBC.SUBJID a Predecessor origin of ADSL.SUBJID, which section ADLBC.SUBJID omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.SUBJID as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines USUBJID give IT.ADLBC.1402-1404 a Predecessor origin of ADSL.USUBJID, which the ADLBC.1402-1404 section projection omits. The derivation is documented; the specification reads LB.USUBJID (adlbc_v1.yaml line 470), a source difference rather than silence.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1444-1446 give IT.ADLBC.TRTSDT a Predecessor origin of ADSL.TRTSDT, which section ADLBC.TRTSDT omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.TRTSDT as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1456-1458 give IT.ADLBC.TRTEDT a Predecessor origin of ADSL.TRTEDT, which section ADLBC.TRTEDT omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.TRTEDT as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1466-1468 give IT.ADLBC.AGE a Predecessor origin of ADSL.AGE, which section ADLBC.AGE omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.AGE as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1478-1480 give IT.ADLBC.AGEGR1 a Predecessor origin of ADSL.AGEGR1, which section ADLBC.AGEGR1 omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.AGEGR1 as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1490-1492 give IT.ADLBC.AGEGR1N a Predecessor origin of ADSL.AGEGR1N, which section ADLBC.AGEGR1N omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.AGEGR1N as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1501-1503 give IT.ADLBC.RACE a Predecessor origin of ADSL.RACE, which section ADLBC.RACE omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.RACE as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1513-1515 give IT.ADLBC.RACEN a Predecessor origin of ADSL.RACEN, which section ADLBC.RACEN omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.RACEN as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1524-1526 give IT.ADLBC.SEX a Predecessor origin of ADSL.SEX, which section ADLBC.SEX omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.SEX as that origin states.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1536-1538 give IT.ADLBC.COMP24FL a Predecessor origin of ADSL.COM01P24FL, which section ADLBC.COMP24FL omits, so the derivation is documented, though under a name ADSL does not hold (section ADSL.COMP24FL). adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.COMP24FL.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1548-1550 give IT.ADLBC.DSRAEFL a Predecessor origin of ADSL.DSR01AEFL, which section ADLBC.DSRAEFL omits, so the derivation is documented, though under a name ADSL does not hold (section ADSL.DSRAEFL). adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.DSRAEFL.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1560-1562 give IT.ADLBC.SAFFL a Predecessor origin of ADSL.SAF01FL, which section ADLBC.SAFFL omits, so the derivation is documented, though under a name ADSL does not hold (section ADSL.SAFFL). adlbc.r lines 96-105 carry ADSL.SAFFL.

ADRG page-12 documents the chemistry scope, but no section file excludes the RETRIEVAL and AMBUL ECG REMOVAL visits that the base-ord filter (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 466-467) drops. CL.VISIT in section ADLBC.VISIT even lists both visits as values.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT names a treatment phase and VISITNUM=12 but lists no eligible visits, and ADRG page-8 says unscheduled visits were used in analyses. The WEEK 2 to WEEK 24 restriction of the base-eot filter (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 818-820) is stated in no section file.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT's 'last assessment of this analyte for the subject' supports the USUBJID and PARAMCD grouping, but no section file says the last assessment is the one with the highest LBSEQ. The LBSEQ descending order of _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 810-817) is therefore undocumented, the same choice AENTMTFL.CR-6.4 records for base-ord.

Section ADLBC.AVISIT attaches a flag method to a visit-label variable and does not define the treatment phase, the discontinuation source or the ordering that makes an assessment last; ADSL.DISCONFL, ADSL.VISNUMEN and ADRG page-12 do not complete it. The cited adlbc.r lines show how the reference was computed and do not document the rule.

Section ADLBC.AVISITN gives only CL.AVISITN code labels such as 0 = Baseline, native define-adam.xml line 1580 gives AVISITN an Assigned origin with no method, and ADRG page-12 names only code 99. No retained text maps LB.VISIT to these codes as adlbc_v1.yaml lines 513-535 do; define-sdtm.xml line 3516 flags LBBLFL when VISIT="SCREENING" but assigns no AVISITN and does not name SCREENING 1.

ADRG page-12 names only the derived end-of-treatment code 99 and CL.AVISITN lists code labels without selecting records, so no document says which LB record becomes the End of Treatment row or how other visits are coded. The cited adlbc.r lines 155-161, 174-182 and 187-197 show the reference computation, not documentation.

Section ADLBC.ADT names LB.LBDTC and ADRG page-45 keeps ADT as a date; completing only the clock time before taking the date (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 481-489) imputes no part of the date. Incomplete or invalid text stays missing, as a plain date conversion of LB.LBDTC leaves it, so no undocumented rule is added.

Native define-adam.xml lines VISIT give IT.ADLBC.1601-1603 a Predecessor origin of LB.VISIT, which the ADLBC.1601-1603 section projection omits. The derivation is documented; the specification copies LB.VISIT (adlbc_v1.yaml line 473).

Native define-adam.xml lines 1634-1636 give IT.ADLBC.PARAMCD a Predecessor origin of LB.TESTCD, which section ADLBC.PARAMCD omits, so the derivation is documented with a misnamed source rather than absent. adlbc.r line 133 copies LBTESTCD.

Section ADLBC.PARCAT1 only lists CL.ADLBCAT (CHEM, HEM, HYLAW) and native define-adam.xml line 1654 gives an Assigned origin with no value, so no document states the constant 'CHEM'. adlbc.r line 135 assigns it, which shows the computation but does not document it.

Section ADLBC.BASE gives Method: LB.LBSTNRHI with no record condition, and native define-adam.xml lines 1767-1771 give ABLFL only a Predecessor origin of LB.LBBLFL, so no retained text states that BASE is the analysis value of the ABLFL = 'Y' record (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 588-591). The 'at baseline' of sections ADLBC.BR2A1LO and ADLBC.BR2A1HI, CL.AVISITN '0 = Baseline' and ADRG page-12 name no baseline flag either.

No define-adam.xml section or ADRG page states which records receive BASE or that the baseline value is carried forward in LBSEQ order within subject and parameter, as _PNM_BASE and _BASE do (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 593-606). Section ADLBC.BASE names only LB.LBSTNRHI, and ADRG pages 17 and 45-48 use LOCF only for ADAS-Cog (ADADAS) records.

Section ADLBC.CHG states AVAL - BASE for every record, and no define-adam.xml section or ADRG page suppresses it on the baseline record. The ABLFL = 'Y' branch at adlbc_v1.yaml lines 382-383 is undocumented, though the CHG.CR-5 evidence is consistent with it.

Section ADLBC.ANL01FL gives an unqualified max(ALBTRVAL), and ADRG page-12 describes the dataset's records without naming the maximum's partition. The USUBJID and PARAMCD grouping of _ANL01_RANK (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 308-310) is stated nowhere.
Section ADLBC.ANL01FL does not restrict the maximum to any visits, and no ADRG page does either. The AVISITN 2 to 24 filter of _ANL01_RANK (adlbc_v1.yaml line 316) is undocumented.

Section ADLBC.ANL01FL assigns only 'Y' under its condition and leaves other records unassigned. The empty text at adlbc_v1.yaml line 421 is that missing character value, not an added condition or category.

Section ADLBC.ANL01FL flags a record only when ALBTRVAL equals max(ALBTRVAL), which a missing ALBTRVAL cannot satisfy under null comparison. The _RANK_VAL IS NOT NULL guard at adlbc_v1.yaml line 419 keeps the rank-based selection to that documented outcome rather than adding a condition.

Section ADLBC.ANL01FL's max(ALBTRVAL) names no partition or eligible records, and ADRG page-12 only describes one record per parameter, time point and subject. The partition, VISITNUM 4 to 12 window and one-record selection of adlbc.r lines 241-251 are program choices no document states.

Section ADLBC.ALBTRVAL says 'Maximum of' two terms without saying what happens when one is missing. greatest at adlbc_v1.yaml lines 620-624 keeps the present term, a missing-value policy no section states.

Section ADLBC.ANRIND's method ends with 'N' as its final else, which is the otherwise 'N' at adlbc_v1.yaml line 637. A missing AVAL meets neither test and reaches that documented 'N', so no undocumented result is added.

Section ADLBC.ANRIND compares AVAL with 0.5*LBSTNRLO directly and says nothing of a missing or zero limit, so the guard at adlbc_v1.yaml lines 626-630 is undocumented. For a zero limit it removes the low result the literal AVAL < 0 test could give, so it is not only a restatement.

Section ADLBC.ANRIND names LBSTRNHI, which no LB variable or ADLBC section defines, and assigns 'Y', which its own CL.LNH excludes. A literal probe cannot read the source as named without a repair; adlbc.r lines 227-228 show a repaired computation, not documentation.

Section ADLBC.BNRIND compares BASE with unqualified limits and does not say which record supplies them or that an indicator is carried forward. The LBSEQ-ordered carry-forward of the baseline record's indicator (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 643-656) is stated in no section.

Section ADLBC.BNRIND ends in 'N' for any BASE its two tests do not catch, so the method gives a missing BASE 'N', not an empty value. The empty BNRIND at adlbc_v1.yaml lines 433-434 is stated nowhere.

Section ADLBC.BNRIND compares BASE with 0.5*LBSTNRLO directly and says nothing of a missing or zero limit, so the guard at adlbc_v1.yaml lines 626-630 is undocumented. For a zero limit it removes the low result the literal BASE < 0 test could give, so it is not only a restatement.

Section ADLBC.BNRIND's low branch assigns ANRIND rather than BNRIND, names the undefined LBSTRNHI and leaves open which record supplies the limits. A literal BNRIND probe needs repairs; adlbc.r lines 227-235 show the reference computation, not documentation.

Native define-adam.xml lines 1767-1769 give IT.ADLBC.ABLFL a Predecessor origin of LB.LBBLFL, which section ADLBC.ABLFL omits, so the derivation is documented. adlbc.r line 143 copies LBBLFL as that origin states.

Section ADLBC.AENTMTFL speaks of the treatment phase and visit 12 but lists no eligible visits, and ADRG page-8 says unscheduled visits were used in analyses. The WEEK 2 to WEEK 24 filter of _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE (adlbc_v1.yaml lines 615-616), which drops unscheduled visits, is stated nowhere.

Within a subject and parameter LBSEQ identifies one LB record (base-eot groups on it with ONLY aggregates, adlbc_v1.yaml lines 665-690), so the LBSEQ order at lines 613-614 leaves row_number no ties to break. row_number picks the single last record section ADLBC.AENTMTFL names; the LBSEQ ordering itself is AENTMTFL.CR-6.4's difference.
